question.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-8 & -8 & -8 \\ -9 & 7 & -4 \\ 3 & -4 & 7\end{bmatrix}
$$

which of the following elementary row operations makes $a_{12}=0$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

At the requested entry, this gives

$$
a_{12}=-8+(-2)\cdot (-4)=0.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 & -8 & -8 \\ -9 & 7 & -4 \\ 3 & -4 & 7\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}-14 & 0 & -22 \\ -9 & 7 & -4 \\ 3 & -4 & 7\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
T=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 5 & -6 \\ 8 & 0 & -9 \\ 7 & -1 & 6\end{bmatrix}
$$

which of the following elementary row operations makes $a_{12}=0$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}.
$$

The entry in row $2$, column $2$ is $0$. Switching rows $1$ and $2$ therefore makes $a_{12}=0$.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T &=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 5 & -6 \\ 8 & 0 & -9 \\ 7 & -1 & 6\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}8 & 0 & -9 \\ -5 & 5 & -6 \\ 7 & -1 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}.
$$
